subject: chem
source: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620) syllabus for examination in 2026, 2027 and 2028 — Cambridge International; Year 11 covers topics 9–12 plus full-course revision for the May/June exams

weeks.topic: Properties and uses of metals
objectives: Compare the physical and chemical properties of metals
Explain the uses of aluminium, copper and steel in terms of properties

weeks.topic: Alloys and their properties
objectives: Describe an alloy as a mixture of a metal with other elements
Explain why alloys are harder than pure metals using structure diagrams
Give uses of brass and stainless steel

weeks.topic: The reactivity series and displacement reactions
objectives: Place metals in order of reactivity using reactions with water, steam and acid
Explain displacement reactions and predict products

weeks.topic: Corrosion of metals: rusting and its prevention
objectives: State the conditions needed for rusting
Describe barrier methods and galvanising
Explain sacrificial protection

weeks.topic: Extraction of metals: iron in the blast furnace
objectives: Relate the method of extraction to reactivity
Describe the reactions in the blast furnace
Explain the removal of impurities with limestone

weeks.topic: Extraction of aluminium by electrolysis
objectives: Describe the extraction of aluminium from bauxite
Explain the role of cryolite and the replacement of carbon anodes

weeks.topic: Water: tests, treatment and pollutants
objectives: Describe chemical tests for water and tests for purity
Describe the treatment of the domestic water supply
Identify substances in water from natural sources and pollutants

weeks.topic: Fertilisers: NPK and ammonium salts
objectives: Explain why plants need nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium
Describe the use of ammonium salts and nitrates as fertilisers

weeks.topic: Air quality and climate: pollutants, greenhouse gases and catalytic converters
objectives: Describe the sources and effects of air pollutants
Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change
Describe how catalytic converters reduce pollution

weeks.topic: Organic chemistry: formulae, functional groups and homologous series
objectives: Draw displayed and structural formulae
Identify functional groups
Describe the features of a homologous series

weeks.topic: Naming organic compounds and structural isomers
objectives: Name and draw unbranched alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and carboxylic acids
Identify structural isomers

weeks.topic: Fuels: fossil fuels and fractional distillation of petroleum
objectives: Name coal, natural gas and petroleum as fossil fuels
Describe the fractional distillation of petroleum
Relate fractions to properties and uses

weeks.topic: Alkanes: combustion and substitution with chlorine
objectives: Describe alkanes as saturated hydrocarbons
Describe complete and incomplete combustion
Describe photochemical substitution with chlorine

weeks.topic: Alkenes: cracking and addition reactions
objectives: Describe cracking of large alkanes
Distinguish alkanes and alkenes with bromine water
Describe addition of hydrogen, steam and bromine to alkenes

weeks.topic: Review: metals, chemistry of the environment, fuels, alkanes and alkenes
objectives: Revise extraction methods and pollutants
Practise organic structure and reaction questions

weeks.topic: Alcohols: manufacture of ethanol and its uses
objectives: Compare fermentation and the catalytic addition of steam to ethene
Describe the combustion and uses of ethanol

weeks.topic: Carboxylic acids and esterification
objectives: Describe the reactions of ethanoic acid with metals, bases and carbonates
Describe the formation of esters from alcohols and carboxylic acids

weeks.topic: Polymers: addition polymerisation and plastics
objectives: Describe addition polymerisation and draw repeat units
Discuss the environmental problems of plastics

weeks.topic: Condensation polymers: polyamides, polyesters and proteins
objectives: Describe condensation polymerisation of nylon and PET
Describe proteins as natural polyamides and their hydrolysis

weeks.topic: Experimental design: apparatus and measurement
objectives: Name appropriate apparatus for measuring time, temperature, mass and volume
Identify variables and suggest improvements to methods

weeks.topic: Acid–base titrations
objectives: Describe the procedure for an acid–base titration
Calculate concentrations from titration results

weeks.topic: Chromatography and Rf values
objectives: Describe paper chromatography and interpret chromatograms
Calculate Rf values
Explain the use of locating agents

weeks.topic: Separation and purification techniques
objectives: Choose between filtration, crystallisation, simple and fractional distillation
Use melting and boiling points to assess purity

weeks.topic: Identification of cations: flame tests and precipitate tests
objectives: Identify metal ions using flame tests
Identify cations using aqueous sodium hydroxide and aqueous ammonia

weeks.topic: Identification of anions and gases
objectives: Test for carbonate, halide, nitrate and sulfate ions
Test for hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, ammonia, chlorine and sulfur dioxide

weeks.topic: Practical skills: planning, results tables and evaluation
objectives: Plan an investigation with a clear method and safety
Draw results tables and graphs
Evaluate sources of error

weeks.topic: Mock exams: full syllabus (multiple choice, theory and practical papers)
objectives: Complete full-length mock papers under exam conditions
Use mock feedback to set revision priorities

weeks.topic: Review: states of matter, atomic structure and bonding
objectives: Revise particle theory and bonding diagrams
Practise structure–property explanations

weeks.topic: Review: stoichiometry and mole calculations
objectives: Practise moles, gas volumes, concentration and yield calculations
Check units and significant figures

weeks.topic: Review: electrochemistry, energetics and chemical reactions
objectives: Revise electrolysis products and half-equations
Practise rate, equilibrium and energy questions

weeks.topic: Review: acids, bases, salts and the Periodic Table
objectives: Revise salt preparations and acid reactions
Practise group trend predictions

weeks.topic: Review: metals and chemistry of the environment
objectives: Revise reactivity, extraction and corrosion
Practise water and air pollution questions

weeks.topic: Review: organic chemistry and chemical analysis
objectives: Revise organic reactions and polymers
Practise ion tests and chromatography questions

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: multiple choice paper (Paper 1 or 2)
objectives: Answer multiple-choice questions efficiently
Check calculations and use elimination

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: theory paper (Paper 3 or 4)
objectives: Answer structured questions with balanced equations and correct units
Show working in calculations

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: practical or alternative to practical paper (Paper 5 or 6)
objectives: Describe methods and identify hazards
Record observations and draw conclusions from data

weeks.topic: IGCSE exams: final exam window and course reflection
objectives: Complete any remaining exam papers
Reflect on the course and next steps for IB or A Level Chemistry
